findings.source_quote: ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστὶν [ὃς] ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ Θεοῦ
findings.english_quote: is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants of God
findings.issue: The English appropriately connects the clauses, but neither its formatting nor note a discloses that the working source brackets the relative pronoun ὃς. This leaves an editorial supplement indistinguishable from unmarked preserved wording. The existing disclosure about διάνοια versus δύναμις addresses a different source issue.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a brief disclosure that the working edition supplies the bracketed relative pronoun translated “who.” The English connective need not be removed or mechanically bracketed; any revised wording or note requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου
findings.english_quote: “Hear now,” he says, “about the spirit that is earthly
findings.issue: The supplied source warning explicitly reports νῦν as an editorial conjecture in the printed apparatus. The English renders it as “now” without disclosing that status, although other working conjectures receive explanatory notes. Retaining the working reading is appropriate; presenting it without its reported editorial status is the disclosure defect.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-qualified note identifying “now” as a working editorial conjecture according to the supplied printed-page review report. Obtain the relevant apparatus transcription before specifying an otherwise-unsupplied witness alternative.

findings.source_quote: ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστὶν [ὃς] ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ Θεοῦ
findings.english_quote: The man on the chair is a false prophet. He destroys the understanding of God’s servants who waver, but not of those who are faithful.
findings.issue: Splitting the sentence is a faithful simplification, but the source disclosure still omits the editorial status of the bracketed relative pronoun ὃς. Note a discusses the understanding/power alternative without identifying this separate supplement.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a short note explaining that the working Greek supplies a bracketed connecting “who,” represented here by a new sentence. Do not characterize that supplied pronoun as unmarked preserved text.

findings.source_quote: τοῖς τοιούτοις πνεύμασιν οὐ κολλῶνται, ἀλλ’ ἀπέχονται ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: They keep away from such spirits.
findings.issue: This preserves the positive distancing clause but drops the explicit negative attachment clause and its contrast: they do not cling to such spirits, but keep away. The distinction matters within this mandate because attachment to the double-minded is also explicitly described in paragraph 13. The standard edition preserves both clauses; the simplified edition does not.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed wording for fresh review: “They do not cling to such spirits. Instead, they keep away from them.”

findings.source_quote: ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου
findings.english_quote: “Now listen about the earthly, empty spirit.
findings.issue: The supplied source warning identifies νῦν as a printed editorial conjecture, but the simplified edition renders “Now” without disclosing that status. Its other conjecture notes do not cover this word.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a brief note attributing the conjectural status of “now” to the supplied printed-page review report. Retain the selected working reading unless a separately reviewed source decision changes it; request the apparatus transcription before giving a specific witness alternative.

summary: Both editions substantially preserve the selected working source, including its difficult assertions, strong exclusions, tests of prophets, and illustrations. The servant wording and provisionally disclosed contextual change-of-mind reading comply with current policy. The substantive understanding/power, prophetic-spirit/prophet, and earthly/holy alternatives are disclosed consistently with the supplied bounded reports; they do not require replacing the working readings. Both editions need two additional editorial-status disclosures, and the simplified edition also omits an explicit negative-and-positive contrast in paragraph 4. This review evaluates the supplied Greek, English, metadata, and reports; it does not authenticate unseen editions or manuscript images, certify exhaustive collation, or automatically approve proposed replacements.
